newsitem.title: UK: LME copper slumps from high by end of volatile day.
newsitem.headline: LME copper slumps from high by end of volatile day.

text.p: A heady concoction of covering against short options and futures positions was enough to send copper prices racing higher in early pre-market trade on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Monday.
But the combination of forward and options-related selling, profit-taking and spread lending finally won the day, pushing the flagship contract well into the minus column by the close.
Three month futures ended the afternoon kerb at $2,026 a tonne, down $13 from Friday's afternoon finish. Cash narrowed to $25/30 over three months, sharply down on $60 late on Friday.
But this was not before three months copper had raced to $2,165, at which point September positions were indicated above the $2,200-a-tonne options strike price.
Options dealers were forced to buy cover ahead of the September options declaration on Wednesday.
"The market raced through two key strikes ($2,100 and $2,200) without touching the sides, but you could hardly buy copper," said one options dealer.
His views reflected wider complaints that the lack of liquidity in early trade had as much to do with the rally as anything else.
One analyst said options had an undue influence over the underlying prices because of the lack of volume.

"When the options market does this it is a case of the tail wagging the dog. The options are supposedly a small market and yet they are having undue influence over the supposedly much bigger futures market," he said.
Options selling was one reason for the big retracement in values as dealers unwound their hedge, traders said.
Volumes did pick up during the morning and afternoon rings in one of the busiest days seen for some time. Cash selling was prominent early on, putting nearby spreads on the defensive.
Other base metals had a relatively calm day, with most edging down by the finish in response to copper's collapse.
Cash selling in all markets during the official rings also pressured values lower across the board.
Aluminium ended at $1,510, down $2 from Friday and $9 below the day's high.
Nickel lost $75 by the close to $7,415 despite having peaked at $7,660 at one stage.
Lead ended firmer, gaining $3 to $815 and supported by physical tightness. Zinc ended up $2 to $1,035 after trading a narrow range all day.
Tin was last indicated at $6,250/60, unchanged from Friday's close of $6,255.
Alloy was last quoted at $1,300/02 from $1,304 at the close on Friday.
